business-data-context · Bunkai TMS

Business data map

Built 2026-10-12 from upex-bunkai-tms origin/staging 98ee1b4 (2026-10-11) and the live database through the read-only QA role. Every fact a figure shows is also in the text.

Overview

What Bunkai is at the data level. Bunkai is a multi-tenant Test Management System. Every row belongs to a workspace (the tenant). Inside it, a team describes the product under test as projects split into a tree of modules, writes user stories with ordered acceptance criteria, and authors ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases: small, reusable checks made of steps and assertions) that must be anchored to a story and at least one of its criteria. ATCs are chained into Tests; a Test is executed as a Run against a project environment; a Run copies the chain at start and records a result per step; failures become bugs. Test plans and milestones organise the work; reports (coverage, traceability, defect heatmap, recovery cycles, run report) are read straight from these tables.

Actors. Browser users (cookie session, roles viewer / member / admin / owner per workspace); programmatic callers (CLI, CI, AI agents) with a personal access token bk_pat_… carrying scopes; three system principals: the pg_cron jobs inside Postgres, the Vercel Cron call to the digest route (bearer CRON_SECRET), and the Stripe webhook (signature-verified).

How data is written. Nearly every business mutation goes through a Postgres function (RPC) that validates, authorises, writes the rows and an activity_log audit row in one transaction. Route handlers under app/api/v1/ call those RPCs either as the user (RLS-scoped client) or through the admin client passing the resolved actor explicitly. Postgres Row Level Security is the authorisation source of truth; there are 38 tables in public, all with RLS enabled, 14 user-defined triggers and two pg_cron jobs.

Value proposition the data enforces. Traceability is structural: an ATC cannot exist without a user story and at least one of that story's criteria, a Run keeps an immutable snapshot of what was executed, and a bug keeps provenance links to the run, failed step and ATC it came from. That chain (criterion to ATC to Test to Run to Bug) is what the traceability and coverage reports read.

Scale in the shared database (dbhub, read-only role, 2026-10-12). about 1,088 workspaces (74 soft-deleted), 1,866 projects, 1,286 user stories, 5,703 ATCs, about 1,356 Tests, 1,350 Runs, 1,755 bugs, 2,295 notifications and about 16,500 activity rows. Most of it is QA and automation test data: 1,074 of 1,109 memberships are owners of their own workspace.

External services. Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Realtime, Storage, pg_cron), Stripe (plan upgrade checkout), Resend (digest and deletion emails), Jira Cloud (one-way story import), Vercel (hosting, background after() workers, the digest cron).

Key relationships

  • A workspace owns projects and Tests directly. Tests are workspace-scoped on purpose: a Test has no project column; its project is derived from the ATCs it chains (test_steps to atcs to projects), so one chain may span two projects.
  • A project owns its module tree, milestones, test plans and environments. Modules hold user stories; a story holds ordered acceptance criteria.
  • An ATC belongs to one project and one module and is anchored to exactly one user story (atcs.user_story_id, ON DELETE RESTRICT) and bound to one or more of that story's criteria through atc_acceptance_criteria (many-to-many). The create and update RPCs reject an empty criteria list and any criterion outside the story.
  • A Test chains ATCs through test_steps by reference, in order; the same ATC may appear at several positions. test_steps.atc_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so a chained ATC cannot be hard-deleted.
  • A test plan holds a Test at most once (test_plan_tests); a Test can be in many plans of the same project.
  • A Run belongs to one Test and one environment (both RESTRICT), snapshots the chain into run_atcs (one per chain position) and run_steps (one per ATC step), and records the module of chain position 1 as runs.module_id.
  • A bug always has a workspace, project and module; its run_id, run_step_id and atc_id are optional provenance links set to null if the source disappears.
  • Notifications and activity rows hang off the workspace; a notification links to its producing activity row through source_event_id.

Workspace and membership

  • Tenant boundary. Every table reaches a workspace_id directly or through its parent; the four RLS helpers (bunkai_is_workspace_member, _admin, _owner, bunkai_can_write_workspace) and the three explicit-actor helpers used by admin-client routes all require an active membership in a live workspace.
  • Creation. bunkai_bootstrap_workspace inserts the workspace and the caller's owner membership in one transaction; the slug is globally unique and a collision is an error, never silently reused. New workspaces start on the community plan.
  • Plan tier (plan: community / cloud / enterprise). The tier ladder lives in TypeScript (lib/billing/plan-tiers.ts): Community 5 seats, 3 projects, 30-day retention, free; Cloud 25 seats, 50 projects, 90 days, 24.00 USD per seat; Enterprise unlimited, custom price. Only the project limit is enforced, by a trigger on projects (see automatic-processes). purchased_seats is written when a Stripe checkout is paid.
  • Soft delete. deleted_at + deletion_requested_by mark a workspace scheduled for deletion; from that instant every helper treats it as non-existent (same refusal as for a non-member, no existence signal). See state-workspace.
  • Membership. role viewer / member / admin / owner; status active / invited / suspended, but only active is ever written by code. Viewers read everything in the workspace and write nothing. A workspace can have several owners; the last owner cannot leave.

Module tree

  • Self-referencing tree with a materialised slash path (for example auth/login), unique per project, depth 1 to 6 enforced by a CHECK. An optional description is capped at 500 characters.
  • Rename rebuilds the path of the module and every descendant in one statement; a sibling slug collision is rejected. Move re-parents and re-bases the subtree, rejecting cycles (new parent inside the subtree), a parent in another project or archived, and any move that would push a descendant beyond depth 6.
  • Archive is the only delete. bunkai_archive_module_subtree stamps archived_at on the module, its descendants, their user stories, criteria and ATCs. Tests, runs and bugs are not touched: a bug filed against an archived module stays readable and is tagged "Archived" on its detail view.
  • Module creation is a plain RLS-checked insert (no RPC, no audit row); rename, description change, move and archive each write an activity row.

User story and acceptance criteria

  • A story belongs to a module and carries a denormalised project_id. external_id (a Jira key) and external_url link it to a tracker; the key is unique per project among active stories, case-insensitive, so an archived story never blocks re-linking.
  • Criteria are ordered by position, unique among active rows; insert, move and archive go through RPCs that rebalance positions atomically.
  • status is draft or ready_to_test. Moving to ready_to_test requires at least one active criterion (serialised with a row lock against criterion archiving); archiving the last active criterion drops the story back to draft. The status is shown in the sidebar and traceability view; no other workflow is gated on it.
  • A story with ATCs attached cannot be hard-deleted (RESTRICT from atcs); the DELETE endpoint archives.

ATC (Acceptance Test Case)

  • Name. The code, UI and app metadata expand ATC as "Acceptance Test Case" (app/layout.tsx, login page, components/atcs/AtcTable.tsx, 0004_atcs.sql).
  • Identity. slug is minted at create as {module-slug}/atc-{8 hex} and never changes; user_story_id and module_id are also immutable on edit.
  • Content. Ordered steps (action, optional input data, expected result) and ordered assertions; both are replaced as a whole on every save. layer is UI / API / Unit; optional technique (Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis, State Transition, Decision Table, Pairwise) and priority (Critical / High / Medium / Low). Title at least 3 characters; at most 10 tags, enforced in the RPC and by a CHECK.
  • Versioning. Every update bumps version and requires the caller's version (optimistic lock, 409 on mismatch). The atc.updated audit row lists the Tests that chain the ATC (affected_test_ids); those Tests show the new content on their next read because they hold references, not copies.
  • Dead column. atcs.status (pass / fail / blocked / skipped / running / unrun) defaults to unrun and no code path writes it: all 5,703 rows read unrun. Execution truth lives in run_atcs.status; coverage reads that instead.
  • Search. A stored tsv column over title and tags (kept fresh by a trigger) backs project-scoped full-text search.

Test (chain of ATCs)

  • A Test is a workspace-scoped header (title 1 to 200 characters, trimmed) plus an ordered chain in test_steps. Creation requires a non-empty chain of ATCs from the same workspace.
  • The chain stores references only. Reading a Test expands each ATC live with its current steps and assertions; the frozen copy belongs to Runs.
  • Reorder must keep exactly the same multiset of ATCs and is guarded by the Test's version. Tags replace the whole set: reserved suite tags smoke, sanity, regression are lower-cased, custom tags keep their casing, duplicates collapse after normalisation.
  • "Used in N tests" for an ATC counts distinct Tests that chain it.

Run (execution snapshot)

  • The header snapshots test_title and the module of chain position 1 at start; executor_mode is human / agent / ci and executor_user_id is the starter (the only recipient of run notifications).
  • run_atcs copies each chain position (ATC title, position); run_steps copies each ATC step (content, input, expected). Links back to the live ATC and step are provenance only and become null if those rows go.
  • Per-step result: status, note, evidence_url, executed_at; updated in place, last write wins, no history.
  • runs has no archive and no delete path; it grows by one row per execution.

Bug

  • Title 5 to 200 characters, severity P1 to P4, optional description and steps to reproduce, up to 10 evidence URLs, reporter (created_by) and optional assignee.
  • Filed from a failed run step (the API derives project, module, run and ATC server-side from run_step_id) or standalone (no provenance; shown as "Filed manually").
  • Consistency is enforced twice: by the create RPC and by the bugs_check_consistency trigger, which rejects a module outside the project, a project outside the workspace, provenance from another project or run, a status that skips or goes backward, and an assignee who is not an active non-viewer member.
  • Bugs have no archive and no delete path.

Activity log (audit and event source)

  • Clients cannot insert: only SECURITY DEFINER RPCs and triggers write it, inside the same transaction as the change, so a failed write leaves no audit row.
  • Actions seen in the database: atc.created, atc.updated, test.created, test.reordered, test.tags_changed, run.started, run.finished, run.aborted, run_step.marked, bug.filed, bug.assigned, bug.reassigned, bug.unassigned, bug.status_changed, module.renamed, module.description_updated, module.moved, module.archived, milestone.created, milestone.updated, test_plan.created, test_plan.updated, test_plan.tests_added, test_plan.test_removed, export.requested, export.downloaded.
  • The activity feed returns a per-action positive projection of the payload, never the raw payload. Terminal run events carry via (cookie or bearer, or sweep) so notification rules can tell an interactive close from an automated one.
  • Two AFTER INSERT triggers turn run and bug events into notifications (see flow-notifications).

Notification and preferences

  • One row per recipient, workspace-scoped, with a payload snapshot (title, project slug, verdict or reason, run id for bugs) so the inbox renders without joining live entities. Unique per (producing activity row, recipient): a replay never double-notifies.
  • A recipient sees only their own rows of the last 90 days while still an active member (RLS). Mark-read is a plain update of read_at.
  • Event types produced: run.finished, run.aborted, bug.assigned, bug.reassigned, bug.status_changed. bug.unassigned reaches the trigger but has no recipient.
  • Preferences are personal and global: run_lifecycle and bug_lifecycle times in_app and email, default on when no row exists; mentions is locked off. Only the email channel is read by code (the digest); the in_app switch is stored but no producer reads it.

Personal access token

  • Shown once as bk_pat_{prefix}.{secret}; only a SHA-256 of the secret is stored, in a sibling secret table the QA inspection roles cannot read. Lookup is by a 12-character prefix.
  • Scopes: atc:read, atc:write, run:execute, workspace:admin (at least one). workspace:admin can only be granted to an admin or owner of the token's workspace; a token with no workspace is global.
  • Issued only from a browser session or by the headless sign-in and confirm endpoints; a PAT cannot mint or revoke tokens. Revocation stamps revoked_at (no delete, for audit). Leaving or deleting a workspace revokes the workspace-scoped tokens.
  • A PAT call acts as its owner: the API mints a short-lived user JWT so RLS sees the same auth.uid() as a browser call.

Workspace invite

  • An admin or owner invites an email with role viewer, member or admin; inviting an existing active member is rejected. The raw token is returned once inside the accept URL; only its hash is stored. Bunkai sends no invite email: the inviter shares the link.
  • State is derived from timestamps, not a status column: pending, accepted (accepted_at), revoked (revoked_at), expired (expires_at, default 7 days after issue). Rotating issues a fresh secret and expiry for the same row.
  • Accepting requires a signed-in user whose email equals the invite email; it adds or upgrades the membership.

Flow: sign-in and first workspace

  1. Email-first entry: POST /api/v1/auth/check-email asks auth_email_status (service role only) whether the account exists and is confirmed. Account existence is knowingly disclosed, mitigated by rate limiting.
  2. Sign-in paths: magic link (POST /auth/magic-link, each link audited in magic_link_tokens), OAuth with GitHub or Google (state cookie, PKCE, /auth/callback), or headless email + password (POST /auth/signin), which also mints a PAT in the same call.
  3. Headless sign-up (POST /auth/signup) creates the user unconfirmed; POST /auth/confirm with the 6-digit email OTP is where the session and a PAT are issued. POST /auth/resend re-sends the code.
  4. First workspace: POST /api/v1/workspaces calls bunkai_bootstrap_workspace (workspace + owner membership, one transaction). This is the one capability-free write a fresh token may do.
  5. The active workspace for the browser is a cookie (POST /me/active-workspace, cookie-only); PAT callers pass the workspace explicitly.

Rules: the sign-in emails are sent by Supabase Auth, not by the app. Side effects: auth.users row, session cookies, PAT row when headless.

Flow: invite, join and leave a workspace

  1. Admin issues an invite (POST /workspaces/{id}/invites); RLS on workspace_invites is the permission check. The response carries the accept URL once.
  2. Admin may rotate (POST …/invites/{inviteId}) or revoke (DELETE, stamps revoked_at).
  3. Invitee signs in and posts the token to /api/v1/invites/accept. Order of checks: token exists, workspace live, then revoked / accepted / expired (409 with a specific message only for live workspaces), then email match. A deleted workspace's invite answers exactly like a token that never existed.
  4. Leaving (DELETE /workspaces/{id}/membership, cookie-only) runs bunkai_leave_workspace: refused when it is the caller's only active workspace or when the caller is the last active owner; on success deletes the membership row and revokes the caller's tokens scoped to that workspace.

Business rules: owner is never an invite role; plan seat limits are shown on the billing page but not checked when inviting or accepting.

Flow: build the project structure

  1. Create a project (POST /workspaces/{id}/projects): a plain RLS insert; the plan's project limit trigger can refuse it. A new project has no environments.
  2. Create modules (POST /projects/{id}/modules), rename, re-describe or move them (PATCH /modules/{id}), archive a subtree (DELETE /modules/{id}).
  3. Add user stories to a module (POST /modules/{id}/user-stories), edit or archive them (/user-stories/{id}), set status draft or ready_to_test.
  4. Add, reorder, edit and archive criteria (/user-stories/{id}/acceptance-criteria, /acceptance-criteria/{id}).

Rules: viewers cannot write; DELETE on modules, stories and criteria archives, never removes rows; structural module changes are audited.

Flow: import user stories from Jira

  1. POST /api/v1/imports with a project and a JQL query (1 to 2,000 characters). Member or above; at most one queued or running import per project (409 import_in_progress, backed by a partial unique index). Returns 202 with the job id.
  2. A Vercel after() worker claims the job (queued to running), pages Jira /rest/api/3/search/jql 100 issues at a time (at most 1,000 pages) with the platform's own Atlassian credentials.
  3. Per issue: description converted from Atlassian document format to Markdown (truncated above 50 KB with a marker), criteria extracted from it, module chosen by Jira component name or an auto-created "Inbox" module, then the story and its criteria are upserted keyed on the Jira key (external_id). Counts created / updated / skipped and per-issue errors are stored on the job.
  4. Job ends completed, or failed on a Jira authentication error or any unexpected throw; it is never left running.
  5. Client polls GET /api/v1/imports/{id}.

One-way only: nothing is written back to Jira. Database: 232 completed and 18 failed jobs.

Flow: author an ATC

  1. POST /api/v1/atcs (scope atc:write) calls bunkai_create_atc: write gate on the project, project derived from the user story, every criterion must belong to that story (45020), the module must be in that project's subtree (45021), at least one criterion, title and tag limits; slug minted; header, steps, assertions and bindings inserted together; atc.created audited.
  2. PATCH /api/v1/atcs/{id} calls bunkai_update_atc under a row lock with the expected version (45022 on conflict), replaces steps, assertions and bindings, bumps the version, audits atc.updated with the affected Tests. The response reports how many Tests are affected.
  3. POST /atcs/{id}/duplicate deep-copies into the same project with a fresh slug and version 1; the copy is a normal atc.created.
  4. Reads: GET /atcs/{id}/usage (Tests chaining it), GET /atcs/search (project-scoped full text over title and tags, filters by module subtree, layer, technique, priority), GET /projects/{id}/atcs/export (whole library as CSV, paged past the 1,000-row REST cap).

There is no ATC delete endpoint; an ATC disappears from the library only when its module subtree is archived.

Flow: compose Tests, plans and milestones

  1. POST /api/v1/tests (idempotency key supported) calls bunkai_create_test: write role, non-empty chain (45120), title rules (45121), every ATC in the caller's workspace (45122); test.created audited.
  2. PATCH /tests/{id}/reorder (same ATCs, new order, version-guarded) and PUT /tests/{id}/tags (replace the tag set, version-guarded). Reads: expanded Test, run history, tag filter, search.
  3. Test plans: POST /projects/{id}/test-plans creates an open plan (name 1 to 100 characters, unique per project ignoring case, goal up to 100, description up to 500). Edits only while open. POST /test-plans/{id}/tests adds Tests whose entire chain lies in the plan's project (45604 otherwise); DELETE …/tests/{testId} removes the membership only.
  4. Milestones: POST /projects/{id}/milestones and PATCH /milestones/{id}; name unique per project ignoring case, whitespace collapsed; target date from today up to 5 years ahead, re-checked only when the date changes, so a past milestone stays editable.

No route closes a test plan and no entity links to milestones yet.

Flow: execute a Test (Run)

  1. Start. POST /api/v1/runs (scope run:execute) with Test, environment and a start_token. A browser caller is always recorded as human; a PAT caller may declare human, agent or ci. bunkai_create_run checks write role, executor mode (45200), that the environment belongs to the Test's project (45201) and that the chain has at least one executable step (45202). The same Test and start token within 24 hours returns the existing running Run instead of a new one. It then copies every chain position and ATC step as pending and audits run.started.
  2. Mark steps. POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark with passed, failed or blocked, plus optional note and evidence URL (blank values become null). Only a running Run accepts marks (45212); pending is never accepted (45213). The step is updated in place and the run ATC verdict is recomputed (figure). Each mark audits run_step.marked. Supabase Realtime pushes run_atcs and run_steps changes to open viewers; the runs row itself is not replicated.
  3. Finish. POST /runs/{id}/finish with verdict passed or failed (45207 otherwise): the verdict is the person's choice, not computed from the steps. Remaining pending steps and run ATCs become skipped, finished_at is set, run.finished audited with via.
  4. Abort. POST /runs/{id}/abort with a reason of 3 to 500 characters: status aborted, pending work skipped, run.aborted audited with the reason and via.
  5. Finish and abort lock the Run row: the first terminal action wins, the loser gets 409 (45206 / 45204).
  6. Filing a bug from a failed step is the next flow.

Business rules: every executor passes the same write gate; the Test template (atcs.status) is never touched by a Run. Side effects: notification to the starter on finish or abort (see flow-notifications).

Flow: file and triage a bug

  1. POST /api/v1/bugs: with run_step_id the server derives project, module, run and ATC from that step; without it the caller supplies project and module (standalone bug). bunkai_create_bug validates module in project (45300), run in project (45305), step in run (45306), ATC in project (45307), title, severity and evidence limits; status starts open; bug.filed audited.
  2. POST /bugs/{id}/assign assigns, reassigns or unassigns: the assignee must be an active member (45312) and not a viewer (45313). Audited as bug.assigned, bug.reassigned or bug.unassigned.
  3. POST /bugs/{id}/status moves exactly one stage forward (45310 when skipping, 45311 when backward or unchanged); audited bug.status_changed with previous and new status.
  4. Reads: project list (filters, keyset paging, severity-first sort, archived modules excluded), single bug with origin (run, failed step position, ATC title and layer) and module archive tag, workspace open-bug counts per severity on Home.

A non-member gets the same not-found as for a missing bug; a member without write role gets forbidden.

Flow: notifications and daily digest

  1. A lifecycle RPC writes its activity_log row. An AFTER INSERT trigger on that table (two of them: run events and bug events) computes recipients and inserts notifications rows in the same transaction.
  2. Recipients. Run finished or aborted: the run starter only, suppressed when the starter closed it from a browser session; a close through a PAT, the sweep or an unknown channel notifies even the starter. Bug assigned or reassigned: the new assignee only (also when self-assigned); the previous assignee gets nothing. Bug status changed: reporter and current assignee, one row each at most, never the person who made the change. Unassigned: nobody.
  3. The inbox (GET /workspaces/{id}/notifications) shows the caller's rows of the last 90 days; new rows arrive by Supabase Realtime. Read one (POST /notifications/{id}/read) or all in a workspace.
  4. Digest: Vercel Cron calls GET /api/v1/admin/send-digest at 08:00 UTC with CRON_SECRET. bunkai_notification_digest_candidates returns unread notifications of the last 90 days for active members of live workspaces, excluding event families whose email preference is off. Per user the route first inserts a pending claim row for the UTC day (a second run skips on conflict), sends one email through Resend, then marks the claim sent or failed. A failed day is not retried; the notifications stay unread for the next day.

Database: 1,173 run.aborted, 194 run.finished, 481 bug.assigned, 67 bug.reassigned and 380 bug.status_changed notifications.

Flow: quality reports

All reports are live, read-only RPCs over the tables above; any active member, viewers included, may read them; a project the caller cannot see answers not found.

  • Coverage (project and workspace). Per criterion: uncovered when no live ATC is bound; not_run when any bound ATC's most recent run result is anything other than passed or failed (no run, pending, skipped, blocked); otherwise executed. A failed ATC still counts as coverage. Per module: no_acs, uncovered, not_run or fully_covered.
  • Story traceability. One call returns a story's chain criterion to ATC to Test to Run to Bug; each run row reads in_flight (run running or ATC still pending), aborted, or the run ATC status; each ATC row carries its module.
  • Run report. A project's runs filtered by status, executor mode, module and start-date range, with pass and fail totals, keyset paged. Test run history: one Test's runs filtered by outcome.
  • Recovery cycles. Per user story, time from the first failing run to the first later all-passing run, from run data only.
  • Defect heatmap. Bugs per active module for a 7, 30 or 90-day window with a week-over-week trend; a parent counts its descendants' bugs, including those filed against modules archived since.
  • Home widgets. Recent projects (latest ATC, module or run activity), active runs, open bugs by severity.
  • Search. The command palette searches six entity types (ATC, Test, Project, Module, Bug, Run) in one RLS-scoped call.

Flow: manage environments

  1. List or add (/projects/{id}/environments): name 1 to 50 characters in the API (60 in the table), unique per project ignoring case.
  2. Rename or delete (/environments/{id}). Delete is a real row delete and is refused while any Run references the environment. An id from another workspace answers not found.

Projects that existed when runs shipped were seeded with Staging and Production; projects created later start with none, and a Run cannot start until one exists. Database: 1,736 of 1,866 projects have no environment.

Flow: upgrade to the Cloud plan

  1. An admin or owner reads the plan overview (GET /workspaces/{id}/billing): plan, purchased seats, active seats, project count, oldest run age; others get 404.
  2. Owner only: POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout (idempotency key, PAT needs workspace:admin) inserts a billing_checkout_sessions row first, at most one open per workspace, then creates a Stripe Checkout Session with that row id as client_reference_id and stores the Stripe session, customer and subscription ids. The user pays on Stripe's hosted page. …/checkout/cancel (owner, on return from Stripe's cancel page) expires the Stripe session and marks the row canceled.
  3. Stripe calls POST /api/v1/billing/webhook. Handled events: checkout.session.completed, …async_payment_succeeded, …async_payment_failed, …expired; others are acknowledged and ignored. bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event finds the row, records the event id for dedupe, and only when Stripe reports paid sets the workspace plan to cloud and purchased_seats. An unknown session answers 5xx so Stripe retries.

Database: 7 checkout sessions, all expired; no workspace is on cloud (1,080 community, 8 enterprise). There is no downgrade, cancellation or renewal handling.

Flow: export workspace data

  1. Owner only, browser session only. POST /workspaces/{id}/data-export enqueues a job; one queued or running export per workspace. A trigger audits export.requested.
  2. A Vercel after() worker claims it, collects projects, modules, stories, criteria, ATCs with steps, assertions and bindings, Tests and chains, Runs with snapshots, bugs, activity and memberships, zips them and uploads to the private Storage bucket workspace-exports; the job becomes completed with size and an expiry 168 hours later, or failed with a message.
  3. GET …/data-export/download re-checks owner, completed and not expired on every request, streams the archive (never a signed URL) and audits export.downloaded.

Flow: delete and restore a workspace

  1. Owner only, browser session only: DELETE /workspaces/{id} runs bunkai_request_workspace_deletion. Other members cannot veto. In one transaction: deleted_at set, all workspace-scoped PATs and pending invites revoked, a workspace_deletions tombstone written (name, slug, requester, purge deadline 30 days later, member count, row-count digest).
  2. After commit, a confirmation email with the restore link goes to the owner and every active member through Resend.
  3. From that moment nobody, owner included, can read or write the workspace through any path; digests stop.
  4. During the grace window the owner can POST /workspaces/{id}/restore: deleted_at cleared, no data moved. Revoked tokens and invites stay revoked.
  5. The daily purge hard-deletes workspaces deleted more than 30 days ago; the cascade removes their data and the tombstone gets purged_at.

Database: 92 tombstones, 16 purged, 74 workspaces currently soft-deleted.

Rules: only running accepts marks, finish or abort; terminal states are final (no reopen). A CHECK keeps abort_reason present exactly when status is aborted. Database: 1,192 aborted (1,157 by the sweep), 105 passed, 53 failed, 0 running.

State machine: run step and run ATC verdict

Values for both: pending, passed, failed, blocked, skipped.

FromToEventEffects

passed / failed / blockedpassed / failed / blockedre-mark while the Run is runninglast write wins; verdict recomputed
pendingskippedRun finished, aborted or sweptno executed_at

Run ATC verdict: pending while any of its steps is pending; then failed if any step failed, else blocked if any is blocked, else passed; still-pending run ATCs become skipped when the Run closes. Database run ATC values: 1,191 skipped, 51 passed, 24 failed, 18 blocked, 5 pending.

State machine: test plan

Values open and closed. Plans are created open and are editable only while open. No RPC, route or UI sets closed (closing is a later story); the table has no client write policy, so a direct update is not a path either. Database: 25 open, 5 closed.

State machine: personal access token

Active until expires_at passes (expired, rejected with a uniform 401) or revoked_at is set (by the owner from a browser, by leaving the workspace, or by workspace deletion). Both ends are final; rows are never deleted. Database: 8,943 tokens not revoked.

Integration: Supabase

  • Postgres holds every business row; RLS plus SECURITY DEFINER RPCs carry the business rules. The QA inspection roles (qa_inspector_ro / _rw) bypass RLS and cannot read the three secret tables.
  • Auth owns users, sessions, magic links, email OTP and OAuth (GitHub, Google). Emails are looked up through two service-role-only functions because auth.users is not exposed.
  • Realtime publishes run_atcs, run_steps and notifications.
  • Storage bucket workspace-exports, service role only.
  • pg_cron runs the sweep and the purge. pg_net and http are not installed, so the database never calls out.

Failure behaviour: the whole product is down without Postgres or Auth; without Realtime, run pages and the inbox stop updating live but writes still succeed; without Storage, exports fail (job marked failed).

Integration: Stripe

Data out: a Checkout Session for the Cloud price (STRIPE_CLOUD_PRICE_ID) with seat quantity and the session row id. Data in: checkout events on the webhook, which change billing_checkout_sessions, stripe_webhook_events and workspaces.plan / purchased_seats. Dependent flow: flow-billing-upgrade. Failure: checkout start fails while Stripe is unreachable; a webhook for a session not yet visible answers 5xx so Stripe redelivers; a delayed payment upgrades only when Stripe reports paid.

Integration: Resend

Outbound email only: the daily notification digest and the workspace deletion receipt with its restore link. Sign-in and confirmation emails come from Supabase Auth, and invites are not emailed. When Resend is not configured or fails, the sender returns a typed failure: the digest claim row is marked failed and the notifications stay unread; the deletion still happens without the email.

Integration: Jira Cloud

Data in only: issues matched by the caller's JQL become user stories and acceptance criteria (flow-jira-import). The app uses one platform-level Atlassian account (ATLASSIAN_URL, ATLASSIAN_EMAIL, ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN), not a per-workspace connection. A Jira authentication failure fails the whole job; other per-issue failures are listed on the job. Stories keep external_id and external_url as the link back.

Integration: Vercel

Hosts the app; after() runs the import, export and deletion-email work after the response is sent; Vercel Cron triggers the daily digest. Vercel registers crons from the production deployment only, so staging has no scheduled digest (it is exercised with a manual POST). If an after() task is lost, its job stays queued: nothing retries it.

Discovery gaps

  • Migration level: the ledger supabase_migrations.schema_migrations and cron.job are not readable by the QA role (permission denied). The applied level was inferred from objects: every public function the 90 snapshot migrations define exists, and the latest bodies of 0089 and 0090 are live, so the database matches the snapshot (origin/staging 98ee1b4). Numbers 0079 and 0080 do not exist in the snapshot; I could not verify whether the ledger has rows for them.
  • Environment: migration headers (0033, 0035, 0058) state that one Supabase project backs local, staging and production. I could not confirm from the database which environment label the dbhub connection represents.
  • Cron jobs: their names and schedules come from migration text only. Evidence the sweep runs: 1,157 runs carry the sweep reason. Purge evidence: 16 tombstones purged.
  • Contradiction with the domain map (built at e88512e): it expands ATC as "Atomic Test Component"; current code, UI and metadata say "Acceptance Test Case" everywhere.
  • Contradiction with the infra map (e88512e): it says there is no vercel.json, no cron and no background worker; the current code has a Vercel cron, two pg_cron jobs and three after() workers. It also lists "shared or separate Supabase project" as unknown (see above).
  • Earlier claim "PAT accepted only on a few routes" is no longer true: the route posture snapshot lists 107 handlers, 74 scope-gated and open to PATs, 9 cookie-only (token issue and revoke, active workspace, leave, data export and download, workspace delete and restore), 9 any-authenticated, 11 public, 4 bypass.
  • Earlier claim "no delete API" is only partly true: 9 routes export DELETE; most archive or revoke, but environment delete, test plan membership removal and the workspace purge remove rows. ATCs, Tests, Runs, bugs, projects, milestones and test plans have no delete.
  • 5 run ATCs are still pending inside closed runs (2 aborted, 1 failed, 2 passed), which finish and abort should have skipped. Origin not verified.
  • 13 Tests have an empty chain although creation refuses one (45120). Origin not verified (direct writes are a guess).
  • 5 test plans are closed although no write path sets it. Origin not verified.
  • 2 memberships have status suspended; no code writes suspended or invited. Meaning not verified.
  • Plan seat and retention limits are displayed as meters but I found no enforcement (invites and acceptance do not check seats; nothing deletes old runs). Whether this is intended is a product question.
  • The in_app notification preference is stored but not read by the notification triggers; only the email preference is applied.
  • Stripe: only checkout events are handled; no subscription cancellation, renewal failure or downgrade path exists, and no workspace has completed an upgrade in this database.
  • Workspace purge: one tombstone is past its purge deadline without purged_at while no workspace qualifies for purge (maybe restored). The purge swallows per-workspace errors; whether RESTRICT foreign keys inside the cascade (runs.test_id, runs.environment_id, test_steps.atc_id, atcs.user_story_id) can make it fail was not verified.
  • Archived ATCs inside a Test chain: how the Test view and run start treat them was not verified.
  • Which Jira site the platform Atlassian credentials point to in each environment: not verified (secret values are not read).
  • notification_digest_log, feature_flags, user_view_state and workspace_exports row counts were not measured (planner statistics empty); flags and view state are read by no code.
  • Run-level live updates: runs is not in the Realtime publication, so a run closed elsewhere is not pushed; UI behaviour not verified.
  • Storage bucket policies were not inspected (the storage schema was not queried).
